lines.speaker: REX
lines.text: Radio Free Fierro. Friends, I've been putting the pieces together. The heat. The ice cream vans. The crime. The lottery. It's all one thing.

lines.speaker: REX
lines.text: And I challenge those so-called scientists in Doherty to prove me wrong. Live, on my show, tonight.

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: He's talking about you, man.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: He's talking about patterns. Some of them are real. That's what makes him convincing.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: So we collect our own observations, put them on a board, and sort the causes from the coincidences.

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: And then we go on the radio with a crazy guy.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: With a crazy guy and a spreadsheet.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: First, the weather. There's a bank thermometer on the beachfront at Ocean Flats.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Thirty-four degrees. Hottest day of the year.

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: No wonder everybody's acting crazy.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Rex says the ice cream vans are everywhere. Let's count a queue. Get a photo.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Twelve people waiting. The driver says sales have tripled since Monday.

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: I'd be in that line if we weren't working.

lines.speaker: DISPATCH
lines.text: All units, high call volume citywide. Disturbances, noise complaints, two car fires. It's a hot one, people.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: And there's the crime half of Rex's chart. Calls are up too.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Rex's favourite: three lottery winners, all on Paradiso Street. Check the board at the newsstand.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Three winners on Paradiso this year. And nine thousand tickets sold there. The biggest seller in the city.

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: So they win more 'cause they play more.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Or Paradiso is magic. Let's put it on the board.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Here's the board. Four connections Rex says are real. You call each one.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Heat and ice cream: a cause. Hot afternoon, people want ice cream.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Heat and ice cream is a cause, Carl. Sales jump the same afternoon the heat does.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Ice cream and crime: common cause. The heat pushes both. Ice cream is innocent.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Ice cream doesn't cause crime. Hot weather pushes both up. If we say that on air, the vans will hear it.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Paradiso and the lottery: coincidence. More tickets, more winners. No magic.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Paradiso isn't lucky. They buy nine thousand tickets. Of course they win more.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: The full moon: can't tell. One month of Rex's chart. Nobody can say from that.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: One month of data from Rex. Honestly, we can't tell either way.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Radio Free Fierro broadcasts from a van on Missionary Hill. Of course it does.

lines.speaker: REXLIVE
lines.text: Well, well. The scientists came. Welcome to the truth, gentlemen. You're live.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Thanks, Rex. You're right that these things go up together. We checked.

lines.speaker: REXLIVE
lines.text: Ha! You hear that, San Fierro? Connected!

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Some of them because one causes the other. Heat sells ice cream.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Some because something else drives both. Heat pushes up ice cream and arguments at the same time.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: And some are just numbers bumping into each other. Paradiso buys more tickets, so it wins more.

lines.speaker: REXLIVE
lines.text: And the full moon?

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: One month of your chart. Nobody can tell from that. Including you.

lines.speaker: REXLIVE
lines.text: ...Hot weather. Huh.

lines.speaker: REXLIVE
lines.text: So what you're saying is, the weather controls us all.

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: That's... not what he said.

lines.speaker: REXLIVE
lines.text: Lines are open, people!

lines.speaker: REXLIVE
lines.text: Breaking news, San Fierro! Vers3Dynamics confirms it: ice cream causes crime!

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: That's not... we didn't... Carl. Look outside.

lines.speaker: TRUCKER
lines.text: Hey! You the guys who said ice cream causes crime?!

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Drive. Drive now.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: I think we lost them. And the ice cream union's goodwill.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Four links. A cause, a common cause, a coincidence and a shrug. That's a good night's science.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Next time we say 'common cause' slower. And louder. Near fewer ice cream vans.

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: Man, that radio guy's gonna be talking about weather control for a year.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Probably. But a few thousand people heard the difference between a cause and a coincidence tonight. That's not nothing.

lines.speaker: NEWS
lines.text: Radio Free Fierro drew record ratings last night with an unusually calm debate about ice cream.

lines.speaker: NEWS
lines.text: Ice cream vans protested outside a Doherty laboratory last night over remarks on pirate radio. No ice cream was harmed.

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: Carl. Tomorrow we open the doors. Everything, in public. Ready?

lines.speaker: CJ
lines.text: Ready for what?

lines.speaker: CHRIS
lines.text: The open experiment.
